subject: Recap + proposed Mutual Action Plan (discovery Mar 14)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@civicahealth.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@civicahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + proposed Mutual Action Plan (discovery Mar 14)

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid overview of how CivicaHealth is evaluating embedding LLMs into your clinical triage workflow. Below is a short recap of what we heard, your goals, and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to keep momentum. Please flag anything I missed or any dates that look off.

Quick summary of pain & goals
- Current pain: triage routing is manual and causes variable wait times; frequent false-priority escalations cost clinical staff time.
- Data constraints: de-identified EHR extracts only; PHI will not be sent to hosted endpoints during pilot (must be VPC/private).
- Success metrics: reduce average triage resolution time by 30% and false-prioritization incidents by 40% during the pilot.
- Non-negotiables: SOC 2 evidence, audit logs, customer-managed KMS for keys.

Proposed MAP (high level)
1) Technical sandbox + security review
   - Owner: Olga (Redwood) / Security: Civica (Priya)
   - Deliverables: security checklist, NDA append, SOC 2 evidences, short demo in private VPC
   - Target: week of Apr 2 — security sign-off by Apr 9
2) Pilot (3 weeks) - controlled sample on de-identified data
   - Owner: Civica engineering (Liam) / Redwood deployment lead (Jonas)
   - Deliverables: pilot config, latency/cost targets, evaluation prompt set, telemetry dashboard access
   - Target start: Apr 10, completion: May 1
3) Executive review & procurement decision
   - Owner: Liam / Priya; Redwood sales (Ben)
   - Deliverable: pilot report, ROI estimate, SOW and procurement paperwork
   - Target: week of May 6, final decision by May 20

Next steps (for this week)
- I will attach a draft MAP and the Redwood security checklist for your review (attached).
- Liam: can you confirm the procurement contact and whether you have an internal PO cadence that affects timelines?
- Priya: please share any additional technical constraints (data egress rules, required DLP controls).

Attachments: CivicaHealth-MAP-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood-security-checklist.pdf (doc stub)

Thanks — I’ll update the MAP and share a v2 with expected owners/dates after your replies.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0118
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@civicahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@civicahealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 16:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed Mutual Action Plan (discovery Mar 14)

Thanks Olga — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Procurement: Sarah Lin (sarah.lin@civicahealth.com) owns vendor onboarding and contracts. I will loop her in once we have the security checklist and a rough SOW.
- Decision process: informal pilot -> exec review -> procurement negotiation. Target approvers are our Head of Operations and CFO.
- Budget: we have a pilot budget approved (internal cap ~$40k) but any committed Dedicated capacity or long-term purchase will need procurement sign-off.
- Data: confirmed — de-identified exports only for pilot; if we move to production we will need a Private deployment option and KMS integration.

One ask: can Redwood provide a short note on how audit logs are retained and an example SLA for latency? That will help Sarah during onboarding.

I’m happy with the proposed dates; Apr 10 start for pilot works for our engineering schedule.

-Liam
